notes.meaning: God created the entire universe out of nothing at the beginning of time. This shows his supreme power and majesty, and it proves that he is completely distinct from what he made. The universe did not come about by chance or exist forever, but was brought into being by the one true God.

At first, the earth was an unformed, dark, watery waste without shape or living creatures. God's Spirit was actively present, hovering over the waters to preserve and prepare them for what was to come. This dark chaos was not an enemy fighting God, but raw material ready to be shaped by his command.

God brought light into existence simply by speaking his powerful word. He needed no tools or outside help, because what he willed happened immediately. In the same way, God brings spiritual light into the human heart when a person is saved.

God looked at the light and approved of it as completely good and suited for his purpose. He then separated the light from the darkness so that each would have its proper place. Light brings life and blessing into the world, while darkness is held within boundaries.

God gave names to the light and the darkness, calling them day and night. Naming them demonstrated his supreme authority over time. The passing of evening and the arrival of morning marked the very first day.

differ.view: Some hold that each day was a normal twenty-four-hour day, while others understand the word day to mean a long period of time.

notes.meaning: God commanded an expanse, or open space, to appear in the midst of the waters. This spread out like a canopy to divide the waters into two distinct parts. It began the work of creating an atmosphere where living things could eventually breathe and live.

God formed this wide expanse and placed a division between the waters beneath it and the waters above it. The lower waters remained on the earth, while the upper waters formed clouds in the sky. Everything was established exactly according to God's command.
God named the expanse sky, showing his complete authority over the heights above the earth. With the close of evening and the arrival of morning, the work of the second day was complete.

God commanded the waters beneath the sky to gather into one place so dry ground could appear. Instead of covering the entire globe, the oceans were gathered into basins by his powerful word. This provided a secure, dry place for land animals and people to dwell.

God named the dry land earth and called the gathered waters seas. He inspected what had been made and declared that this arrangement was good. By setting clear boundaries for the waters, God protected the earth from returning to chaos.

God commanded the earth to bring forth all kinds of plant life, including grass, seed-bearing plants, and fruit trees. These plants were designed to reproduce their own kinds through seeds. Even though plants grow from the soil, they sprouted solely by the power of God's word.

The earth obeyed God's command and produced rich vegetation, seed-bearing plants, and fruit trees. Each plant carried the ability to multiply its own species across future generations. God looked over all the green growth and saw that it was good.
Evening passed and morning arrived, bringing an end to the third day. During these first three days, God shaped the unformed world and made it ready to support life.

God commanded lights to appear in the expanse of the sky to divide the day from the night. These lights were appointed to serve as signs to mark off regular days, years, and religious seasons. They provide an orderly schedule for life on earth and for worship.

These heavenly lights were assigned to shine down upon the earth and give it necessary brightness. God set them as permanent light-bearers so the world would have light to sustain living creatures. Everything happened just as God spoke.

God made the sun to rule the day, the moon to rule the night, and all the stars. These heavenly bodies are not gods to be worshiped, as ancient pagans thought, but creations made to serve human life. They are called great lights because of how brightly they shine to people on earth.
God placed the sun, moon, and stars in the sky to shine down on the earth. He set them at the right distance so their light and heat would bless the earth without harming it.

These lights were appointed to preside over the day and night and to separate light from darkness. God observed their faithful, orderly operation and saw that it was good. Their daily cycles demonstrate his continual care over creation.
Evening closed and morning dawned, marking the end of the fourth day. God had now filled the skies with lights, answering the general light he called forth on the first day.

God commanded the waters to swarm with swimming creatures and told birds to fly through the open sky. This was the first time animal life was called into existence. By God's word, water and air were filled with an enormous variety of living creatures.

God created large sea creatures along with every moving water animal and every kind of bird. Even the giant creatures of the deep are not rival monsters, but things made by God that live under his authority. God looked upon these swimming and flying creatures and saw that they were good.

God blessed the sea creatures and birds, commanding them to be fruitful and multiply. This divine blessing gave them the ongoing power to reproduce and preserve their species throughout history. Their abundance is a direct result of God's generous gift.
Evening fell and morning arrived, concluding the fifth day. Both the oceans and the skies were now populated with living beings according to God's plan.

God commanded the dry land to bring forth living creatures according to their kinds. This included tame animals suited for farm work, wild animals, and small creatures that creep on the ground. Each creature was designed to produce its own kind without blending into another.

God made every kind of wild beast, farm animal, and crawling creature by his almighty power. They did not appear by blind chance, but were individually crafted by God's wisdom. God looked at all the land animals and declared that they were good.

God took special counsel before his final work, saying, 'Let Us make man in Our image.' Human beings were created to be God's visible representatives on earth, ruling over all other creatures with care and justice. This unique design gives every human life supreme worth and dignity.

God created human beings in his own image, making them male and female. This image includes an immortal soul, the ability to know and love God, and moral purity. Both men and women share equally in this reflection of God's character.

God blessed the first man and woman and told them to have children, fill the earth, and govern it. He placed them as stewards, or caretakers, over all the fish, birds, and land animals. People were given the duty to care for the earth under God's supreme authority.

God provided food for human beings, granting them every seed-bearing plant and fruit tree across the earth. In this initial state of creation, humanity was given crops and fruits for daily nourishment. This shows God's faithful care to supply all our physical needs.

God also provided green plants as food for all land animals, birds, and creeping things. Every creature with the breath of life was given plant nourishment so that all lived in harmony without preying on each other. Everything came to pass exactly as God willed.

God reviewed everything he had made during the six days and declared that it was very good. Every part of creation was complete, harmonious, and suited to fulfill the Creator's purpose. Evening and morning marked the close of the sixth day, ending the work of creation.
